mcq.s: On the occasion of which festival did Jayaprakash Narayan escape from Hazaribagh Jail in 1942?
mcq.x: During the Quit India Movement JP escaped from Hazaribagh Jail with his comrades on Diwali night, 9 November 1942.

mcq.s: 'Operation Rubicon' was the code word proposed to be adopted by the British Government in India with reference to:
o: Gandhi's fast unto death in jail
Gandhi's participation in the Round Table Conference
mcq.x: During Gandhi's 21-day fast in the Aga Khan Palace (February 1943), 'Operation Rubicon' was the secret plan to be put into effect if he died.

mcq.s: Which of the following countries did not recognise the Azad Hind Government?
mcq.x: The Azad Hind Government (1943) was recognised by Japan, Germany, Italy, Thailand, Burma, the Philippines, Manchukuo, Croatia and the Wang Jingwei government of China; Indonesia was not then an independent state.

mcq.s:
Which of the following were the main events of the year 1945?
1. Wavell Plan
2. Shimla Conference
3. Naval Mutiny
4. INA Trial
mcq.x: Wavell Plan (14 June 1945), Shimla Conference (25 June-14 July 1945) and the INA trials (November 1945) were in 1945; the Naval Mutiny was in February 1946.

mcq.s: At the Congress Working Committee meeting at Allahabad (April-May 1942), who secured a majority for his plan of guerrilla war against the Japanese, in line with India's unequivocal stand against Nazism, Fascism and imperialism?
mcq.x: At the Allahabad CWC of 1942, Nehru carried his view that Japanese aggression should be resisted, including by guerrilla war, because of the Congress's stand against Fascism and imperialism.

mcq.s: Who held the office of Speaker both in the Central Legislative Assembly of the British era and in the Parliament of free India?
mcq.x: G.V. Mavalankar was President (Speaker) of the Central Legislative Assembly from January 1946 and became the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha (1952-56).

mcq.s: As an alternative to the partition of India, Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that he:
o: Invite Jinnah to form the Government
Invite Nehru and Jinnah to form the Government
Invite the army to take over for some time
mcq.x: In his first meetings with Mountbatten (March-April 1947) Gandhi proposed that Jinnah be asked to form the government, to avert partition; the Congress leaders rejected it.

why: answer not certain (who voted against partition at the AICC, June 1947)

mcq.s: Who sang Iqbal's 'Saare Jahan Se Achha' and 'Jana Gana Mana' in the Central Assembly at midnight of 14/15 August 1947?
mcq.x: At the midnight session of 14-15 August 1947 in the Constituent Assembly (Central Hall), Sucheta Kripalani sang 'Saare Jahan Se Achha', 'Jana Gana Mana' and 'Vande Mataram'.

mcq.s:
Match List-I (War) with List-II (Period):
A. Second Anglo-Mysore War
B. Second Anglo-French (Carnatic) War
C. Second Anglo-Maratha War
D. Second Anglo-Afghan War
List-II: 1. 1803-05  2. 1780-84  3. 1878-80  4. 1749-54
mcq.x: Second Anglo-Mysore War 1780-84; Second Carnatic War 1749-54; Second Anglo-Maratha War 1803-05; Second Anglo-Afghan War 1878-80.

mcq.s:
Match List-I (Event) with List-II (Year):
A. Treaty of Allahabad
B. Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
C. La Bourdonnais's capture of Madras
D. Dupleix's dismissal
List-II: 1. 1754  2. 1746  3. 1748  4. 1765
mcq.x: Treaty of Allahabad 1765; Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle 1748; La Bourdonnais took Madras in 1746; Dupleix was recalled in 1754.

mcq.s:
Match List-I (Person) with List-II (Commission headed):
A. Andrew Fraser
B. Antony MacDonnell
C. Colin Scott-Moncrieff
D. Thomas Robertson
List-II: 1. Famine Commission  2. Irrigation Commission  3. Police Commission  4. Railway Commission
mcq.x: Under Curzon: Fraser Police Commission (1902-03), MacDonnell Famine Commission (1900-01), Scott-Moncrieff Irrigation Commission (1901-03), Robertson Railway Commission (1901-03).

mcq.s:
Arrange the following battles in chronological order:
I. Battle of Mudki
II. Battle of Porto Novo
III. Battle of Shakarkheda
IV. Battle of Bedara
mcq.x: Shakarkheda 1724, Bedara 1759, Porto Novo 1781, Mudki 1845.

why: trivia about a college principal (W.A.J. Archibald)
world GK (first woman PM in the world)

mcq.s: On which date did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the maker of the Constitution of India, die?
mcq.x: Ambedkar died on 6 December 1956 at his home in Delhi (observed as Mahaparinirvan Diwas); he was given the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990.

mcq.s: In which year did Rabindranath Tagore die?
mcq.x: Tagore (born 7 May 1861) died on 7 August 1941 at his ancestral home in Calcutta.

mcq.s: Who called Rabindranath Tagore 'the Great Sentinel'?
mcq.x: Gandhi called Tagore 'the Great Sentinel'; Tagore in turn is credited with calling Gandhi 'Mahatma'.

why: key wrong and no correct option (Bharatiya Kisan Sangh was founded in 1979)

mcq.s: The statement "I am a socialist and a republican and am no believer in kings and princes" is associated with:
mcq.x: Nehru said this in his presidential address at the Lahore Congress, 1929.

mcq.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
I. Assassination of Curzon Wyllie
II. Execution of Khudiram Bose
III. Starting of 'Kesari' by Bal Gangadhar Tilak
IV. Starting of 'Al-Hilal' by Abul Kalam Azad
mcq.x: Kesari 1881; Khudiram Bose hanged 1908; Curzon Wyllie shot in London 1909; Al-Hilal 1912.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
mcq.x: Hicky started Hicky's Bengal Gazette (1780), not the Calcutta Chronicle; the other pairs are correct.

mcq.s: The Banaras session of the Hindu Mahasabha in August 1923 was presided over by:
mcq.x: Madan Mohan Malaviya presided over the August 1923 Banaras (Varanasi) session of the All India Hindu Mahasabha.

why: Bihar local history (creator of modern Bihar)

mcq.s: How did the study of history help in creating a feeling of nationalism in India towards the end of the 19th century?
o: By urging people to struggle and change the miserable conditions under British rule
By reinterpreting history and refuting the British portrayal of Indians as backward and incapable of self-rule
By writing about India's glorious past and urging people to take pride in it
mcq.x: Nationalist historians wrote of India's glorious past, refuted the British view of Indians as backward and urged people to struggle against colonial rule.

mcq.s: Dr. Rajendra Prasad belonged to:
mcq.x: Rajendra Prasad was born on 3 December 1884 at Ziradei (Siwan district), Bihar; he was the first President of India.

why: ambiguous: Panchsheel and peaceful coexistence are also Nehru's

mcq.s: Which of the following is the correct chronological order?
o: Non-Cooperation Movement, Nehru Report, Simon Commission, Quit India Movement
Non-Cooperation Movement, Simon Commission, Nehru Report, Quit India Movement
Non-Cooperation Movement, Nehru Report, Quit India Movement, Simon Commission
Nehru Report, Quit India Movement, Simon Commission, Non-Cooperation Movement
mcq.x: Non-Cooperation Movement 1920-22, Simon Commission 1927, Nehru Report 1928, Quit India Movement 1942.

mcq.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
(i) Formation of Naujawan Bharat Sabha
(ii) Formation of Swaraj Party
(iii) The Dandi March
(iv) The Jallianwala Bagh tragedy
mcq.x: Jallianwala Bagh 1919, Swaraj Party 1923, Naujawan Bharat Sabha 1926, Dandi March 1930.
